messages.author: a424a73546ce9bc7
messages.subject: Problems with an external package
parts:
Hi
I am having problems using an external package "gdxrrw" (from http://support.gams.com/gdxrrw:interfacing_gams_and_r, version 0.5.4. 
I did the following:

packrat::set_opts(local.repos = "D:/EDV/software/R_local")

Then put the tar.gz as well as the zip file and also unzipped the files. 

I tried to install it using (I tried packrat::init() but that gave me errors, so I tried to install it using packrat):

packrat::install_local("gdxrrw")

I first tried:

packrat::init() 

and got the following message:

In read.dcf(...) :  cannot open compressed file 'D:/EDV/software/R_local/gdxrrw', probable reason 'Permission denied

Then I tried installing the package using

packrat::install_local("gdxrrw")

And got the following error messages:

Failed to run system command:

"C:/PROGRA~1/R/R-32~1.2/bin/x64/R" --vanilla CMD INSTALL "D:\EDV\software\R_local\gdxrrw" --library="C:/emacs/home/R/win-library/3.2" --install-tests 

The command failed with output:
* installing *binary* package 'gdxrrw' ...
cp: unknown option -- )
Try '/usr/bin/cp --help' for more information.
Warning: running command 'cp -R . "C:/emacs/home/R/win-library/3.2/gdxrrw" || ( internal cd - .| (cd "C:/emacs/home/R/win-library/3.2/gdxrrw" && internal -xf -))' had status 1
ERROR: installing binary package failed
* removing 'C:/emacs/home/R/win-library/3.2/gdxrrw'

Any help is welcome!

Cheers
Renger

messages.author: ab0d2be2ea8dabe8
messages.subject: Re: Problems with an external package
parts:
Although I'm not positive, it looks like you placed a binary package, rather than a source package, in your external library. Currently, packrat expects to only see package sources, not unpacked binaries, in that folder.

FWIW, I would recommend using a local CRAN-like repository over the 'external library' method -- please see the documentation at https://rstudio.github.io/packrat/custom-repos.html, and also ?"repository-management" if you're using the latest version of packrat on GitHub.

Thanks,
Kevin
